command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 4 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -netdev user,id=net0 -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=net0,disable-legacy=on' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-lock-current-smp4-verified-2026-11-11.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-demo-lock
target: AArch64 QEMU virt with four requested vCPUs and the current desktop ISO
checks: QEMU was invoked with four vCPUs requested; both expected unlocked/locked count rows were visible in the GUI, terminal recovery returned 42, and zstatus reported failed=0.
This validates the Lock demo and recovery path on the ARM64 bridge's single modeled CPU only; it does not exercise simultaneous inter-CPU lock contention.

The ARM64 runtime binds mp_count to guest_mp_count=1, and TaskBridge.ZC documents JobQueue as CPU-0-only; requesting four QEMU vCPUs does not establish ZealOS SMP scheduling or inter-CPU lock contention.
scope_note: Diagnostic only. The ARM64 task bridge is currently a single modeled CPU with cooperative CPU-0 jobs. Full SMP support, vCPU discovery, per-CPU executive/task structures, cross-CPU job dispatch, and genuine unlocked-versus-locked contention remain unimplemented and unverified.
